claims.claim: U.S. law‑enforcement agencies revealed that a North‑Korean state‑sponsored hacking group stole more than $400 million in cryptocurrency by luring victims into fabricated video meetings.

State-sponsored hackers from North Korea have taken more than $400 million in cryptocurrency by using fake video calls to steal people's identities, US authorities say. "North Korean cyber actors have used the FaceStealer scheme to aggressively target individuals in the cryptocurrency and Web3 sectors through deceptive social engineering tactics, resulting in the theft of more than $400 million in the last 18 months."

claims.evidence: The US has seized servers linked to a North Korean scam that used fake video meetings and deepfakes to steal more than $400 million in crypto, and has moved to seize $1.2 billion that was taken from Binance. "North Korea's government bankrolls its rogue regime and illicit weapons program through cryptocurrency theft," said M. Scott Proctor, the department's principal deputy assistant attorney general for national security. North Korea has denied involvement in the Binance hack. AP put the figure at about $6.3 billion (5.7 billion euros) and called it the biggest crypto heist on record. The FBI says hackers are also starting to use AI-generated deepfakes of well-known crypto figures. "If you can't imagine a scenario where you might fall prey to it, you are not thinking creatively enough," said Patrick Grandy, who heads the FBI's Los Angeles field office. Under a federal warrant, the FBI seized more than 900 webcam videos of victims. It is separate from the North Korean military hackers blamed for the Binance theft.
